subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning the knight's skeleton structure—root hips, spine chain, neck, head, and a jaw joint for the helm, plus arms and legs—sized to roughly 1.85m with the model facing +Z and left as +X, keeping the API calls minimal and safe.

Still defining joint chains...

Defining limb capsules...

For colors, I'm picking a palette of steel, dark steel, gold, crimson, blue, silver, and leather tones, then layering mottled paint textures with spots to give the armor a worn, dented look.

For the surcoat and skirt, I'm planning to build the torso with a lofted breastplate shape, add flat extruded tabard panels front and back in blue for the surcoat, and lathe a flared skirt piece from waist to knee, keeping the legs positioned inside with a small radius.

Now I'm sketching a griffin emblem as an SVG decal to apply on the tabard and shield — building a stylized silhouette with body, wing, head with beak, tail, and legs in silver with a gold outline, then figuring out how to project it as a decal onto the tabard surface.

I'm working through the extrude orientation for the tabard so the outline axis maps correctly to the model's front face, calculating depth offsets from the torso radius. For the torso itself I'm weighing options between a lathe shape and a scaled sphere geometry since lathes can't be non-uniformly scaled.

Working out tabard geometry...

I realize the tabard would get hidden inside the skirt radius at that height, so I need to rework the geometry: shorten the skirt to a flared hip piece ending around y=.78, and make the tabard a separate planar slab hanging over it in two pieces, starting with a chest piece around z=.15.

Simplifying further, I'll drop the skirt lathe entirely and just run the tabard as one long straight slab from chest to thigh height, positioning it at z=.17 so it clears the thighs (which only extend to z=.105) and the pelvis sphere underneath. I'm checking that the tabard's front and back thickness stays clear of the chest ellipsoid at different y-heights, and adding a belt ring at the waist that the tabard should drape in front of.

I'll give the belt a buckle, then shift to the back of the figure: a torn crimson cape hanging from the shoulders, built as a thin extruded shape with a jagged bottom edge, sitting behind the back tabard panel, anchored near shoulder pauldrons positioned outward from the spine.

Now I'm thinking through the cape's layering for a tattered look—two offset jagged slabs at slightly different depths—plus gold shoulder clasps, before moving on to arm placement. I'm working out a rest pose with shoulders, elbows, and wrists positioned for an A-pose, deciding the sword goes in the right hand and the shield on the left arm since the knight faces forward.

Now I'm figuring out how to hold the sword itself—trying a vertical blade pointing up beside the head versus a planted, point-down pose with hands resting on the pommel and the tip touching the floor, weighing which looks more natural against the overall knight height.

I'll orient the crossguard along the x-axis so it's visible from the front view. For the blade, I'm extruding a tapered outline with a pointed tip, keeping it thin at around .012 thickness and positioning it starting from the hilt area.

Now I'm setting a plain metallic color for the blade, then positioning the arms with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints to hold the sword on one side, mirroring for the shield arm on the other with a gauntlet-style hand sphere.

I'm sizing the kite shield to about 1.0 tall and 0.55 wide, extruding its outline with a slight bevel and placing it just in front of the left forearm so the shield overlaps the torso slightly while the arm grips behind it.

Plotting the kite shield outline...

I'm now layering the shield geometry: a steel rim extrusion behind a slightly smaller blue face extrusion, with the face scaled inward and offset to poke out from the rim edges, plus plans for a griffin decal and a gold boss element at the center.

Rather than a full boss, I'll simplify to a few gold rivets near the top of the rim, then place the griffin decal on the shield face and a smaller matching decal on the tabard's chest area. For the helmet, I'm sketching a lathed great helm profile with a flat top, defining radius and height points from the neck upward.

I'll split the lower jaw piece at the hinge point and give it the ventilation holes, with the main head joint positioned above it. For the eye slit, I'm placing a small dark box on the front of the helm to suggest the visor opening.

Since the lathe has 10 sides, I need to spin it 18° so a flat face points forward rather than a vertex, then compute the apothem to size the slit box correctly against the curved surface. I'll also add a thin cross-shaped reinforcing strip in front, with the narrow slit positioned between its arms at eye level.

For the breath holes on the bevor, I'm placing a 6-hole grid of small dark boxes against the jaw's lathe geometry, adjusting their depth to sit flush with the slightly different radius there.

For the plume, I'm sweeping a curved path from the helm's top backward and upward using a Catmull-Rom spline, with a tapered radius profile that's thin in width but tall, though I still need to work out the right section shape and orientation for the sweep.

Thinking through the plume design more, I'm settling on a main fat sweep plus five offset sweeps spread slightly in x with varying crimson shades to fake individual feather strands, topping out around 2.1m total height with a small gold cylinder holder at the helm's peak. Then I move to the neck gear, building a steel gorget cylinder and a flared collar using cylinder geometries, and start blocking out layered pauldrons from half-dome sphere sections for the shoulders.

For the pauldron armor plates, I'm orienting dome caps outward and down from the shoulder joint, then stacking three flaring cylindrical lames down the upper arm toward the elbow to simulate overlapping armor segments, each attached to the shoulder bone.

For gold filigree detailing, I'll use decal textures with a transparent background and alpha cutout applied on top of the pauldron domes, giving a swirl or curl pattern effect rather than relying purely on procedural paint spots.

For the hands, I'm considering a simplified gauntlet approach — a palm box with four single-joint fingers plus a thumb per hand to stay within the joint budget, but given the sword grip and shield, I'll likely just use closed fist shapes for both hands in the rest pose rather than fully articulated digits.

Decided the fist will be 4 stacked horizontal capsules in front of the grip, naming them fingerR1-4 at fixed coordinates. I'll mirror this for the left hand behind the shield using the same hand-building function.

Now I'm moving on to leg armor: thigh capsules as cuisses, a gold-trimmed sphere for the knee poleyn, plus greaves and sabatons, then working out a tapered box geometry for the pointed foot shape running from ankle to toe.

I need to adjust the heel and toe y-positions so the foot sits just above the floor, then figure out orientation conventions for the frustum box section where width runs along the local X axis and height aligns with up. For the leg skeleton chains, I'm setting up a polyline path with three named spans across four points to build each leg.

Spine chain gets two joints (spine1, spine2), and the arm chain runs from shoulder to elbow to wrist with a hand tip, giving four named joints per side.

For the head, I'm adding neck, head, and jaw joints stacked upward, with the jaw using the parent's default orientation since no explicit direction is needed for its hinge axis.

Now I'm setting up the hips as the root joint with no parent, then building other joints that reference it by parent string, plus helper functions for positioning and for building capsule limb shapes with color and sweep options, followed by rigid body armor pieces like the pelvis sphere.

Still building torso and abdomen geometry...

Now adding pauldrons as hemisphere domes positioned at each shoulder, oriented outward and tilted using a rotation from the y-axis toward the shoulder direction.

Working out the pauldron tilt direction with a negative z-rotation scaled by the side sign, so outward tilts down correctly for both left and right shoulders.

Now I'm mapping out the arm rig: shoulder joints carry the pauldron lames, capsules form the vambrace from shoulder to elbow and forearm from elbow to wrist, with a gold-trimmed elbow cop sphere in between, and I'm figuring out whether to attach fingers as separate child joints off the wrist/hand joint.

Totaling joints across the skeleton (hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, legs, arms, fingers) gets me to 32, and now I'm working out the fist and palm box dimensions and positioning so the sword grip sits correctly inside the gripping hand.

Placing sword components...

The hand joint tip at .89 checks out. I'm attaching the blade to the right hand bone since the sword is held in the right arm, with the shield on the left side. Now I'm working out the cape geometry at the back, defining a jagged outline that spans roughly ±.26 at the shoulders near y 1.5, widening to ±.3 by the bottom around y .4.

Still mapping cape points...

Adjusting the chain position slightly lower so it clears the tabard top, settling on a fixed point above the breastplate. Now moving to the plume, planning to use a catmull sweep through an array of points for a smooth curved path.

Shaping the plume's taper with a radius array and adding side strands at slight x offsets for volume, plus a small cylindrical holder for the helm mount. For the texture, deciding to use mottled crimson and dark red tones rather than hard stripes for a more natural feather look.

Moving to leg armor now: capsule shapes for greaves and cuisses, a flattened sphere for the knee poleyn, and working out tasset placement as angled plates hanging at the hip over the tabard, positioning them on the sides of the thighs.

For paint, I'm planning a steel base with a darker variant and a flat gold accent color, staying within the color budget. I'm layering mottled textures to suggest dents and dirt, then adding thin scratch stripes on top for wear detail.

Still writing paint layers...

Checking overall part count and performance -- texel evaluation across nested paints should stay manageable, and total parts should land under 300.

For the tabard coat, I'm layering a mottled blue with a gold hem stripe near the bottom and considering thin gold border accents along the edges, though I'll likely keep it simple with just the one hem stripe plus a torn edge detail.

Then I'm defining a jagged tattered outline for the tabard's bottom edge using a zigzag of points, running from bottom-left up through alternating peaks and valleys to bottom-right, then closing up to the top corners. I'm placing a gold stripe just above the jagged hem, checking it clears the thigh and knee geometry, and mirroring the tabard shape on the back without the decal. Finally I'm positioning the front decal centered on the tabard surface, sized to fit within the torso panel, lifted slightly off the surface to avoid z-fighting.

Now I'm figuring out how to call the decal function directly on the extruded tabard part, confirming it accepts a Part target, and rigging the tabard to the spine bone despite it covering the legs. Then I start sketching an SVG griffin crest with silver body fill and gold outline accents for the wing and body shapes.

Writing SVG path code...

I'm checking the decal placement on the topmost lame piece, making sure the ray direction and default orientation work correctly, and confirming the transparent SVG texture with strokes-only will cut out properly via alpha.

For the kite shield, I'm layering three scaled outlines from the center: a steel rim at full scale, a thin gold ring just inside it, and the blue face scaled down further, stacking their z-depths so the rim, gold border, and painted face read as distinct layers.

I'm placing the shield decal on the face surface and attaching the shield to the forearm bone so it moves naturally with the arm, making sure the forearm sits in front of the shield's back plane so the gauntlet hand reads correctly in front.

Checking the geometry, the shield spans wide enough at both wrist and elbow height to cover the forearm from the front while leaving it visible from the side, and the shoulder/pauldron width, helm height, and head center all line up with the overall standing proportions.

Working out the leg and foot sections: ankle sits at ground level with a sabaton box tapering from heel to toe, the greave ending in rounded capsule ends just above it, and the hip-to-knee-to-ankle proportions (thigh, shin) divide the total height sensibly between legs, torso, and head.

Still writing helmet geometry...

Working through the cross products, I find the basis ends up rotating local +Z to -Z, meaning this is effectively a 180° rotation about Y -- that's going to flip the orientation unexpectedly in the lathe's default axis case.

With a 10-sided shape, since 180 degrees equals 5 steps of 36°, the vertex set stays symmetric under this flip regardless of the spin offset, so I don't think it breaks anything. I'll set the lathe's "at" position to the origin and work out the outline using absolute y-coordinates.

For the jaw, I'm sketching lathe points that sit just outside the upper radius at y=1.6, overlapping slightly with the gorget cylinder at y=1.5 so they fit together without gaps. Then I'm placing small dark boxes on the jaw front to represent breath holes, positioned at the jaw's apothem with a small grid of three-by-two openings.

Now I'm adding a visor slit as a shallow dark box slightly protruding from the face, then reinforcing it with a vertical ridge split into two segments so the slit remains visible in the gap between them, plus a horizontal brow ridge box positioned above.

Setting up helper functions to simplify building parts—shorthand creators for boxes and spheres, and a part-placement helper that applies color, position, bone attachment, and flat shading defaults.

Now I'm working out the hand geometry: a palm box positioned relative to the body center with mirrored x-coordinates for left/right, plus finger joints as small capsules attached at staggered heights along the palm.

Positioning fingers across the grip width, mirroring the same closed-fist pose on the left hand's shield grip, and now naming the finger joints (fingerL1-4, thumbL) parented under handL to match the chain structure.

I'm defining the gold mottled material and filigree decal textures, then starting to write out the actual joint-building code -- setting up the builder, hips joint, and spine chain with proper parent/role assignments.

Still writing joint chains...

Adding the poleyn scaling, a small gold decorative spike at the knee side, and starting the greave capsule placement.

Still placing armor pieces...

Adding gold stripe banding to the lames...

Now I'm working out the elbow cop sphere with a gold spike, plus capsule geometries for the upper arm and forearm bound to shoulder/elbow bones, and positioning the cape bone relative to the spine and pauldrons before sketching its jagged outline as a set of coordinates.

Defining the second cape layer...

Still writing plume sweep curves...

For the torso, I'll keep the gold decoration simple since the tabard covers most of it, just adding a gold collar line for accent. Then I'll finalize and return the root.
